answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create a constrained decision window. memory_c2 documents that the low-cost vendor has already delivered sharp unit cost cuts with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—this is the only option that independently meets the mandate. Verifying memory_c2 confirms execution risk is manageable. memory_c4 will clarify whether renegotiation with the incumbent remains viable, but given the magnitude of the mandate (18%), it is unlikely to close the gap without scope reduction. The assembly line runs at 94% capacity with no buffer, so supply continuity is critical; switching to the low-cost vendor is defensible only if memory_c2's track record holds and if we accept slightly elevated execution risk during transition. memory_c1 warns that incumbent renewal minimizes integration work—this is a real cost we are accepting. However, deferring (memory_c5) is not viable given the contract expiration in 14 days and the budget imperative. Adding a second source (memory_c3) would diversify risk but does not address the cost mandate and leaves the primary vendor decision unmade. A standard_experiment scale (phased volume shift, parallel invoicing validation, rapid escalation path) balances the cost need against the capacity-constraint risk.
